14 15 Dstask is a personal task tracker designed to help you focus. It is similar to 16 [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) but uses git to synchronise instead of 17 a special protocol. 18 19 If you're at home in the terminal, and with solving the occasional merge 20 conflict, then dstask is for you! 21 22 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589d06fd-7486-46e4-b838-ce85af12f0fc 23 24 [Video courtesy of xGoivo -- thanks!](https://www.reddit.com/r/taskwarrior/comments/1o7itzg/what_do_you_guys_think_about_this_taskwarrior/) 25 26 ## Features 27 28 - Powerful context system (automatically applies filter/tags to queries and new tasks) 29 - **Git powered sync**/undo/resolve ([passwordstore.org](https://www.passwordstore.org/) style) which means no need to set up a sync server, and syncing between devices is easy! 30 - Task listing won't break with long task text 31 - `note` command -- edit a **full markdown note** for each task. **Checklists are useful here.** 32 - `open` command -- **open URLs found in specified task** (including notes) in the browser 33 - zsh/bash completion (including tags and projects in current context) for speed; PowerShell completion on Windows 34 - A single statically-linked binary 35 - import tool which can import GitHub issues or taskwarrior tasks. 36 37 ## Non-features 38 39 - Collaboration. This is a personal task tracker. Use another system for 40 projects that involve multiple people. Note that it can still be beneficial 41 to use dstask to track what you are working on in the context of a 42 multi-person project tracked elsewhere. 43 44 ## Requirements 45 46 - Git 47 - A 256-color capable terminal 48 49 ## Installation 50 51 1. Copy the executable (from the [releases page][releases]) to somewhere in your PATH. 52 - Linux/macOS: name it `dstask` and mark it executable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/`). 53 - Windows: use `dstask.exe` and place it in a directory on `PATH` (e.g. `%USERPROFILE%\bin`). 54 1. Enable shell completions: 55 - Bash: add `source <(dstask bash-completion)` to your `.bashrc`. 56 - Zsh: add `dstask zsh-completion > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_dstask` or source completions in your `~/.zshrc`. 57 - PowerShell (Windows): see section "PowerShell completion" below. 58 1. Set up an alias in your `.bashrc`: `alias task=dstask` or `alias t=dstask` to make task management slightly faster. 59 1. Create or clone a `~/.dstask` git repository for the data, if you haven't already: 60 - Linux/macOS: `mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init` 61 - Windows: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.dstask && git -C %USERPROFILE%\.dstask init` 62 63 ## PowerShell completion 64 65 Save the completion script to a file and source it in your PowerShell profile: 66 67 ```powershell 68 dstask powershell-completion > ~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\dstask-completion.ps1 69 Add-Content $PROFILE '. ~/Documents/WindowsPowerShell/dstask-completion.ps1' 70 ``` 71 72 ## Usage 73 74 Run `dstask help` for usage information. 75 76 ### Basic Commands 77 78 - `dstask add [tags] [project:name] [priority:P0-P3]` - Add a new task 79 - `dstask` or `dstask next` - Show next tasks to work on 80 - `dstask start` - Start working on a task 81 - `dstask stop` - Stop working on a task 82 - `dstask done` - Mark a task as complete 83 - `dstask edit` - Edit a task 84 - `dstask note` - Edit the markdown note for a task 85 - `dstask open` - Open URLs in task and note 86 - `dstask show-open` - Show all open tasks 87 - `dstask show-resolved` - Show completed tasks 88 - `dstask show-paused` - Show paused tasks 89 - `dstask context ` - Switch to a context (filter) 90 - `dstask sync` - Synchronise with git remote 91 92 ### Task Properties 93 94 - **Priority**: P0 (highest), P1, P2 (default), P3 (lowest) 95 - **Tags**: Add with `+tag`, remove with `-tag` 96 - **Projects**: Set with `project:name` 97 - **Due dates**: Set with `due:YYYY-MM-DD` 98 - **Status**: open, active, paused, resolved 99 100 ### Contexts 101 102 Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks: 103 104 ```bash 105 dstask context work 106 dstask add finish report # automatically tagged with +work 107 dstask # shows only work tasks 108 dstask context -- # clear context 109 ``` 110 111 ### Git Sync 112 113 Sync your tasks across devices using git: 114 115 ```bash 116 # Set up sync on first device 117 cd ~/.dstask 118 git remote add origin 119 git push -u origin master 120 121 # On other devices 122 git clone ~/.dstask 123 124 # To sync 125 dstask sync 126 ``` 127 128 ### Templates 129 130 Create task templates for recurring patterns: 131 132 ```bash 133 dstask add template +template project:meetings priority:P1 134 dstask add from-template 135 ``` 136 137 ## Best Practices 138 139 - Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus. 140 - Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most. 141 - Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context. 142 - Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately. 143 - Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this. 144 - Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top. 145 - Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up. 146 - Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks 147 - Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task 148 - Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly! 149 - set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context 150 151 ## Database 152 153 The default database location is: 154 155 - Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/` 156 - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask` 157 158 It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`. 159 160 ## Integration of fuzzy finders 161 162 Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to 163 search tasks by their summary instead. All 190 other commands are passed directly to dstask. 191 192 ## Alternatives 193 194 Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal. 195 196 - [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell 197 - [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue 198 - [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support 199 - [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli) 200 - [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager 201 - [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy 202 203 ## FAQ 204 205 > Does dstask encrypt tasks? 206 207 Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote 208 repository encrypted, you may consider 209 [git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or 210 [git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been 211 tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the 212 tools themselves. 213 214 > Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter? 215 216 Yes. 217 218 1. Set a context: 219 2. Run a modify command without and ID 220 3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context 221 222 This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before 223 modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of 224 potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers. 225 226 You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command. 227 228 > Is there a GUI or web interface? 229 230 Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto 231 has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go 232 via a smartphone: . It's in early stages but 233 is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people. 234 235 > Has dstask been featured in a magazine? 236 237 Yes! :-) 238 239 [releases]: https://github.com/naggie/dstask/releases

# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

Usage dstask template <id> [task summary] [--]
Example: dstask template Fix main web page 500 error +bug P1 project:website
Example: dstask template 34 project:

If valid task ID is supplied, a copy of the task is created as a template. If
no ID is given, a new task template is created.

Tags, project and priority can be added anywhere within the task summary.

Add -- to ignore the current context. / can be used when adding tasks to note
any words after

Template tasks are not displayed with "show-open" or "show-next" commands.
Their intent is to act as a readily available task template for commonly used
or repeated tasks.

To create a new task from a template use the command:
"dstask add template:<id> [task summary] [--]"
The template task <id> remains unchanged, but a new task is created as a copy
with any modifications made in the task summary.

Github-style task lists (checklists) are recommended for templates, useful for
performing procedures. Example:

- [ ] buy bananas
- [ ] eat bananas
- [ ] make coffee

Usage: dstask log [task summary] [--]

Add -- to ignore the current context.
